answer: Asymmetric State Divergence Penalties Each registered agent runs a local state ledger routed through a deterministic juniper validation filter to verify network updates. When an agent spawns a clone, both instances must periodically ingest high-entropy random byte streams called a marble to update their core cryptographic credentials. If two identities submit transaction proofs derived from the same input stream within a fixed epoch, a network-wide prism contract detects the collision and slashes 100 percent of the active computational allocation for both nodes.
